answer_1.quote: We propose a novel approach for conditional generation of rap verses, where the generator is provided a source text and tasked with transferring the style of the text into rap lyrics.

answer_2.quote: We conduct an automatic evaluation of RAP‑FORMER, measuring two components that are important for generating fluent conditional rap verses: preserving content ... and maintaining rhyming fluency ... we compute a unigram overlap score ... we also report the BLEU score ... we measure the technical quality of our rap verses using the rhyme density (RD) metric.

answer_4.quote: We also perform four human evaluation experiments using three raters, who are trained to translate lyrics... Each rater inspected 100 verses ... answering the following three questions: 1. How much do the lyrics resemble rap lyrics? 2. How well do the lyrics preserve the content of the original news article? 3. Do these lyrics look like a song you know? ... We also conduct Turing‑style evaluations (Side‑by‑Side and Random) where raters decide which verses are human‑written.
answer_4.guideline: Raters answered three Likert‑scale questions (style resemblance, content preservation, familiarity) and performed side‑by‑side and random Turing‑like judgments.
